about: Pinned data for scripts/check-predicate-consumers.py (issue #323 class). Edited by hand on purpose; there is no --update mode.

predicates: upstream Linux-session predicates, resolved WITHOUT minified names - by an un-minified namespace member (find.namespaceKey) or by the definition's shape (find.bodyRegex, named group 'name' = local name; find.prefilter = a literal the definition contains; expectDefinitions when upstream ships copies). The script hard-requires the tracked set.

predicates[].definitionShape: regexes anchored at the definition's body that match OUR injected start or || operand; a match covers the predicate at its definition, i.e. every alias. predicates[].transitiveIgnore: callees (matched by body shape, with a reason) that cannot decide the result on Linux; a predicate is transitively covered only when its body is covered tracked calls and those callees joined by boolean operators.

coveredSites: OUR exact injected shape around one consumer ('@@' marks the consumer's reference), with a pinned consumer count and a reason. decides: 'opt-in' = our term decides only while a user switch is on; reported as opt-in-site, not covered.

allowlist: consumers that stay upstream on purpose, keyed by a stable anchor (string literal, log tag or un-minified namespace name; anchorRegex for a [\w$]+ shape) in the consumer's function (scope 'function', default) or its own statement (scope 'statement'), with a pinned consumer count, a verdict (intentional | upstream-ok | open, open needs an 'issue') and a reason. via: omitted = the root predicate's own consumers; 'derived' = consumers of any derived value (a chunk-level NAME=<expr of predicate>, or a function whose single return is the predicate expression); '<NAME>' = consumers of the derived value exported under that un-minified name.

envSites: upstream occurrences of XDG_SESSION_TYPE / WAYLAND_DISPLAY / XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP / ozone-platform outside every tracked definition and outside our own injected code, with a pinned count and a reason.

A new or widened allowlist / coveredSites / envSites / transitiveIgnore entry or definitionShape, a raised count, decides: 'opt-in' or via: 'derived' loosens the gate: it needs @patrickjaja in the commit.

predicates.about: XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP classifier -> kde | gnome | other; one copy in the main chunk, one in index.pre.js
!isWaylandSession(); gates the device-bridge (cloud Cowork / Dispatch) computer tools and the approval card's app icons

transitiveIgnore.reason: isMacosBelowComputerUseFloor: darwin-only term (false on Linux), so it never decides the result here.

allowlist.reason: sableOtter (paste helper) skips Wayland upstream; not a Computer Use path.
Feature status of the same sableOtter helper: unavailable on Wayland, matching its Wayland skip.

Upstream's executor choice (portal vs X11) right after our globalThis.__linuxExecutor early return: reached only when our executor failed to install, and then upstream's own choice is the right fallback.

Exi(), called once at module load. On every Wayland session it installs (1) the webContents input guard (computer-use/linux/waylandInputGuard), which drops input only while upstream's own Wayland executor has an injection in flight - those counters are raised only from upstream's portal executor (B-NXT-PY chunk) - and whose keyDown Escape hook calls upstream's CU abort (in-window Escape stop, wanted); (2) the dialog counter around dialog.show*, read only by upstream's Wayland executor; (3) cuLockChanged -> stop the portal session and the will-quit token persist, both no-ops without an upstream portal session (restore token undefined); (4) the share-ended callback registration, fired only by upstream's portal session. Our injected executor replaces upstream's, so none of these change behaviour. The Escape work's share-ended capture (fix_computer_use_linux 17c) hooks the callback where it is declared, not this function, so nothing of ours runs here.
Clipboard restore after CU: on Wayland upstream restores through its portal clipboard, which falls back to Electron's clipboard when no portal session exists (our executor's case).

allowlist.anchor: Computer use on Wayland needs a desktop portal
allowlist.reason: computerUse feature status: unreachable on Linux, the isCuSupportedPlatform arm (covered, true on Linux) returns 'supported' before it, and 'not enabled for this account' precedes it otherwise.
Quick Entry registration waits for main-window focus on Wayland (portal shortcuts need a focused window). Documented; our --toggle path does not depend on it.

App-ready awaits the GlobalShortcuts portal probe (CLn) and the RemoteDesktop/Clipboard portal probe (TLn) before continuing; both resolve false at once off Wayland. The GlobalShortcuts probe is our documented Wayland hotkey design (Quick Entry --toggle, KDE rebind); the RemoteDesktop probe only feeds upstream's own portal executor, which ours replaces.
Startup warm-up calls of the same two portal probes (GlobalShortcuts, RemoteDesktop/Clipboard); results are cached, nothing is decided here.

globalShortcut registration refuses when the GlobalShortcuts portal is absent on Wayland ('global shortcuts usable' wrapper); our Quick Entry --toggle path and the KDE rebind patch are the documented answer.
quickEntryGlobalShortcut feature status built from the same 'global shortcuts usable' wrapper; truthful (the portal decides), same design as above.

allowlist.anchor: [cu] app enumeration failed, tool description will omit list
allowlist.reason: Reads only PLATFORM_CAPABILITIES.platform, which is 'linux' in every Linux preset.

CU tool definitions (Code/Cowork session server and the device-bridge tools) spread the static preset: on Linux both arms carry screenshotFiltering 'none' (Wayland upstream, X11 via fix_computer_use_linux sub-patch 2b); what each backend really filters is told by our consent text and prompt suffix, not by this preset.
Enable-prompt card's hostPlatform: reads only PLATFORM_CAPABILITIES.platform, 'linux' in every Linux preset.

Upstream's Electron glow window needs a click-through always-on-top window, unavailable on Wayland; X11 shows upstream's glow, KDE Wayland draws the bridge's own layer-shell glow (kwin-portal-bridge session_overlay), GNOME has the portal's screen-share indicator.
Action-label overlay: compiled off on every platform in this build (returns false regardless of the predicate).
Window-state persistence listeners skipped under ozone Wayland (Electron cannot read/restore positions there).

allowlist.anchor: mainView bounds were stale on focus
allowlist.reason: Main-window creation: the maximize/full-screen restore flag and the Wayland border-radius handlers (both in the same function). Window-chrome behaviour, no Computer Use relevance.
Feature list resolves supportsTrayIcon (StatusNotifier host probe under ozone Wayland / GNOME); truthful, our tray patches build on it.

allowlist.anchor: Quitting app on main window close since this desktop shows no tray icon
allowlist.reason: Closing the main window quits when no tray host exists (otherwise the app would be unreachable); upstream's behaviour is right on Linux.
Pop-out title bar overlay is not available under ozone Wayland (Electron limitation); no Computer Use relevance.
KWallet preflight only on KDE.
index.pre.js: picks the kwallet password store on KDE before app ready.
Keyring name in the no-keyring notice text only.
Tray flavour diagnostics in a crash report (passes the classifier as a value).

Tray icon flavour: GNOME gets the dark glyph. Our 'Always use the white tray icon' switch (globalThis.__cdbTrayAlwaysWhite) overrides it only when ON; with the switch off upstream's GNOME rule applies, which is the intended default.
Chrome import reads the browser keyring from KWallet on KDE, Secret Service elsewhere.

GNOME-only (XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP) suppression of upstream's bare-Alt-tap app-menu popup (flag 1550954491, gated by 1116624256) in the main-window before-input-event handler; window UX, not a Wayland or Computer Use path; flag left at the upstream default (template comment only).

coveredSites.reason: Wayland system-prompt suffix (per-app-truth A, 16a): on Linux our spSuffix() text returns before upstream's arm; upstream's text stays only as the fallback when js/cu_consent.js is missing or throws.
computerUsePerAppAccess (per-app-truth B): on Linux our __cdbCuSharedScreen() decides; upstream's Wayland test only when that helper is missing.

'Entire screen' pseudo-grant (16d): on Linux it is left out in kwin mode or while ask-before-control is on (__cdbCuNoScreenGrant() true); our term only ever removes it, otherwise upstream's preset test adds it.
Enable-prompt card (16e, session server and local agent canUseTool): on Linux, when __cdbCuSharedScreen() is false, the live executor's screenshotFiltering (mask / native) replaces the preset's none.

Teach-mode getter getChicagoTeachModeEnabled (7d), rewritten at its definition: on Wayland (CLICK_THROUGH_WINDOWS false) our term enables teach mode exactly when the kwin bridge drives the teach overlay; X11 keeps upstream's click-through overlay. Covering the getter's own read means its consumers inherit it.

Community switch 'Escape stops Computer Use' (add_feature_cu_escape_abort, default off): with it on and a watcher armed, our watcher replaces upstream's Escape register; with it off, or when no watcher can run, upstream's path runs untouched by design, its Wayland skip included.

envSites.reason: SSH child env: clears SSH_ASKPASS when a display is set (DISPLAY or WAYLAND_DISPLAY); no gate.
Environment allow-list regex for child processes (passes WAYLAND_DISPLAY through); no gate.
Env-var schema registry (WAYLAND_DISPLAY: string); names only, no test.
Telemetry: raw session type reported as linux_session_type; nothing is decided by it.
Telemetry: raw desktop reported as linux_desktop_environment; nothing is decided by it.
Tray crash diagnostics (xdg_current_desktop_set); nothing is decided by it.

Ours: fix_builtin_mcp_browser_env appends its EXTRA_VARS list (DISPLAY, WAYLAND_DISPLAY, ... KDE_SESSION_VERSION) to upstream's env pass-through list in the main and device-tools chunks. This first entry's left context is upstream's list, so the both-sided ours check cannot claim it; names only, no test.

Ours: fix_computer_use_linux's Code-tab access text picks the kwin/Wayland wording (globalThis.__cuKwinMode||XDG_SESSION_TYPE==='wayland') in front of upstream's fallback text; it sits at the boundary with upstream's string, so the both-sided ours check cannot claim it.
